passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text lists her as a Senate principal coauthor; operative Sec. 220.5 forbids school rules requiring disclosure, and Sec. 220.3 only removes any duty to disclose rather than mandating secrecy, so rung 1 is excluded.
passages.actor_quote: Senators Atkins, Eggman, Laird, Menjivar, Padilla, and Wiener

passages.note: Senate floor final passage of the Senate-amended text, 29-8 (not near-unanimous); she voted Aye.

rows.reasoning: Menjivar was a Senate principal coauthor of AB 1955 (2023-2024) and voted Aye on its Senate final passage (29-8); its operative Section 220.5 bars schools from enacting or enforcing any policy that would require staff to disclose a pupil's gender identity without the pupil's consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; it does not go as far as "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents", since Section 220.3 only says staff shall not be required to disclose.
